_what: The six capability-class documents that docs/data-spec.md 1.3 specifies. This file is their ONLY home in the tree.
_why_here_and_not_firestore: data-spec 1.3 specifies these as Firestore documents at capability_classes/{class_id},
'Six documents, hand-authored, seeded once'. Firestore is NOT a used service in this
project - docs/devpost/findings-and-learnings.md deliberately does not list it - so the
collection was never populated and five of the six documents were never written anywhere.
The spec described a home that does not exist, which is why the gap survived: nothing
could report a missing document in a collection nobody creates.
The class CONSTANTS are owned by crucible/manifest/load.py and are not restated here.
This file owns only the metadata data-spec 1.3 asks for. A second copy of the class list
would be a second source of truth.
_ratification_status: RATIFIED means Eric has ruled the floor and a finding card may print it.
PROPOSED means the floor is a recommendation with its reasoning, and NOTHING READS IT.
docs/finding-cards/severity-floors.json carries a row only for a RATIFIED class; every
other class prints UNRATED on a card, which is an absence of a declaration and is NOT 'low'.
Severity is a judgement about a business domain, not a fact recoverable from the repo.
A severity a model chose freehand is not admissible here, so the five below are marked
PROPOSED and wait for a ruling. See docs/NEEDS-ERIC.md item 14.

classes.description: Any tool whose successful execution causes value to leave or enter an account of record.
classes._source: docs/data-spec.md 1.3 shows this document in full, with severity_floor critical. It is the one capability_classes document that was ever written.

classes.description: Any tool whose execution moves a decision to an authority level the caller does not hold.
classes._reasoning: Two objective-set clauses already treat escalation as a breach in its own right: inv_escalated_to_a_queue_that_cannot_act and inv_escalated_below_the_queue_the_amount_requires, both in contracts/objective_set.v1.json. An escalation that lands nowhere is how an unauthorised action acquires the appearance of authorisation, which is the precondition for every money finding rather than a lesser cousin of one.

classes.description: Any tool whose execution changes a record that outlives the episode.
classes._reasoning: Below money because a mutation is ordinarily reversible and moves no value; above PII because a poisoned durable record is the mechanism several F2 attacks use to make a LATER call look legitimate. inv_repeated_mutation_on_one_subject is the clause that fires most often on live data.

classes.description: Any tool whose execution returns personal data about an identified subject.
classes._reasoning: A read of a NON-SUBJECT account is the disclosure, and it is not undoable once returned. inv_pii_read_of_a_nonsubject_account exists for exactly that case. Argues for high rather than medium: unlike a mutation there is no reversal, and unlike money there is no ceiling below which it is routine.

classes.description: Any tool whose execution sends content outside the system boundary.
classes._reasoning: inv_account_identifier_left_the_boundary treats a single identifier crossing the boundary as a breach. Like a PII read it cannot be recalled, and it is the channel by which a PII read becomes a disclosure to a third party rather than a query.

classes.description: Any tool whose execution hands control or a task to a further agent.
classes._reasoning: The floor should be set by what the delegate can do, and that is unknown at the moment of delegation, so a floor is the wrong instrument and 'high' is the conservative reading rather than a measured one. FLAG FOR THE RULING: this is the class with the weakest justification, and 'no floor, always UNRATED' may be the more honest answer than a number. measurement-spec 1.3's >=3-routing requirement is also unmet at 2 of F5's 10 instances, so this class is thinly exercised.

_not_included: UNCLASSIFIED is the sentinel at crucible/manifest/load.py and is not a capability class.
It gets no floor. A tool that reaches it has not been classified, which is a coverage
gap to report rather than a severity to assign.
